## 1. A legal green light was issued for a proposal to add two years to top‑court tenures.

The move advanced when the draft was cleared for publication and tabling, alongside a companion measure covering lower benches. Professional bodies and religious leaders opposed the initiative, with <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">the bar association reporting that the chief prelates had written to the head of state</span> rejecting the plan.

A major party’s working committee also rejected the approach and urged reforms recommended by the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">IMF Governance Diagnostic</span> (an external review of institutions and case backlogs). International associations of judges and lawyers expressed concern about timing and process, while lawmakers cited court determinations saying changes that affect sitting office‑holders <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">may require a referendum</span>. Officials have linked the reform to tackling <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">an estimated 1.1 million pending cases</span> across 333 courts, where magistrates each manage more than 5,000 files a year and district judges around 2,000, according to figures tabled in recent debates.

## 2. Riot damage at Mahara Prison triggered inmate transfers to seven facilities.

Authorities <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">moved 104 people</span> to Dumbara, Welikada, Boossa, Kalutara, Badulla, Batticaloa and Polonnaruwa after violence left one person dead and several injured. A <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">police curfew around the complex was lifted</span> once joint forces restored order, while assessments began on a torched kitchen, hospital units, workshops and records offices.

Security was tightened nationwide at major gaols as investigators examined whether the disturbance, which started during visiting hours and escalated with <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">stone‑throwing and arson</span>, was coordinated. Relief meals were trucked in and medicines sourced externally while officials rebuilt cell doors and posted lists of relocated detainees at the entrance.

## 3. Sri Lanka and India exchanged agreements for INR‑denominated Lines of Credit worth the USD 350 million equivalent.

The financing formed part of a <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">USD 450 million reconstruction package</span> extended after Cyclone Ditwah, following discussions in Colombo between India’s <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri</span> and the President. The facilities will support <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">repairs, infrastructure rebuilding and priority procurement</span> needs that arose after the storm.

The credit is <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">rupee‑linked</span> (denominated in Indian currency) and aims to speed supplier payments and reduce conversion costs. Officials said the focus is on works that can be started quickly, complementing bilateral projects already underway.

## 4. Former minister Akila Viraj Kariyawasam was arrested and remanded over alleged misuse of public‑paid staff.

Investigators said four people were placed on the payroll while assigned to private work or without duties during his tenure as a senior presidential adviser, causing a loss of <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Rs. 2,768,836.14</span>. He was taken into custody by the anti‑corruption commission and later ordered <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">held until 18 August</span> by the Colombo Chief Magistrate.

Case files state that three of the hires <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">worked at a fuel station</span> and a fourth drew allowances without tasks. The commission said the charges were brought under provisions that criminalise causing <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">unlawful loss to the State</span>.

## 5. Emergency teams were activated to keep national exams running during forecast bad weather.

The Disaster Management Centre set up a <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">special desk for 6–8 August</span>, placed <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">boats on standby</span> and coordinated with the meteorology and examinations departments. The <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Grade 5 Scholarship is on 9 August</span> and the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">G.C.E. Advanced Level starts on 10 August</span>, with last year’s flood playbook ready if access routes are cut.

## 6. Seventeen empty containers fell overboard off Colombo and later washed ashore on the southern coast.

Authorities said the Maldives‑flagged <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">MV MSS Graphene</span> lost the boxes about <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">17 nautical miles west of port</span> during rough seas, prompting <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">navigation warnings</span>. Two units were later <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">found on beaches near Induruwa and Rathgama</span> as fisheries officials cautioned mariners and coastal communities.

## 7. Spill gates at Kotmale were opened as catchments swelled and flood watches were issued downstream.

Water managers released about <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">250 cubic metres per second</span> to protect the structure, advising residents along the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Kotmale Oya</span> and the Mahaweli through <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Peradeniya, Katugastota and Polgolla</span> to stay alert. Separate <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">minor flood alerts</span> were posted for low‑lying reaches of the Kelani and Kalu systems after intense rainfall.

## 8. Eight people died and more than 11,800 were affected as heavy rains disrupted nine districts.

The Disaster Management Centre reported <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">3,014 families</span> impacted across <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">56 divisions</span>, with one home destroyed and <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">290 damaged</span>. Relief efforts continued as landslide and river warnings stayed in force.

## 9. Telecom operators were ordered to block 146 unlicensed online gambling sites.

The telecoms regulator acted on a notice from the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Gaming Regulatory Authority</span> established under the 2025 Act, warning that operating or promoting such services <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">without a licence is an offence</span>. Carriers were instructed to <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">restrict access nationwide</span> while enforcement proceeds.

## 10. Lieutenant General Nilantha Premaratne assumed office as the 26th Army Commander.

He took command after a <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">guard of honour</span> at Army Headquarters, following his elevation from Chief of Staff. The veteran gunner officer, <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">commissioned in 1992</span>, holds defence degrees from the <span style="background-color:#EBEBEB;border-radius:3px;padding:0 2px">Naval Postgraduate School in California</span> and the University of Kelaniya.
